title: What should a short-stay property owner see in a monthly report?
description: A practical checklist for reviewing short-stay bookings, channel payouts, expenses and property work without mistaking gross booking value for owner income.
intro: Ask for a report that lets you trace each booking from the channel statement to the amount received and the costs paid. A headline occupancy or revenue figure alone cannot explain what reached the owner. Agree on the report format, timing and supporting records with a prospective manager before relying on it.

sections.heading: Can I match each stay to the money received?
sections.html:
Start with a booking-level schedule: property or room, booking channel, stay dates, booking reference, status and the amount actually paid out. If a reservation was cancelled, changed or refunded, show that separately rather than folding it into a headline total. For private-room properties, identify the booked room; do not report three room bookings as three whole-apartment stays.

Ask how the manager ties its figures to the channel’s own statement or payout record. Airbnb, for example, lets hosts review earnings by listing and payout method and download reports. The exact statements available depend on the channels and account permissions in use.

sections.heading: Which costs should be visible beside booking revenue?
sections.html:
Request a clear breakdown of channel charges, management fees, cleaning, consumables, maintenance and any other agreed costs. Label each amount as charged, paid or still pending. This helps distinguish the guest-facing booking total, a channel payout and the amount ultimately due to the owner; those are not automatically the same number.

For unusual expenses, ask for the date, reason, approval route and invoice or receipt. A report should also show credits or reimbursements so a later adjustment is not mistaken for new booking income.

sections.heading: What should the report say about property condition?
sections.html:
A financial table cannot show whether an apartment is being looked after. Ask for a concise log of completed cleaning, reported damage, repairs and unresolved maintenance, with dates and supporting evidence where appropriate. Separate a guest issue from work in common or strata-controlled areas, and identify who is responsible for the next action.

Agree in advance which decisions the manager can make without contacting you, what spending needs approval and how urgent safety or access problems will be escalated. The manager questions guide covers the broader service scope before you sign.

sections.heading: How do I use the report without treating it as tax advice?
sections.html:
Keep the underlying booking, income and expense records, not just a polished summary. The Australian Taxation Office advises keeping records for rental property income and expenses and separating records by property. Ask your accountant which records and allocations apply to your ownership and use of the property; a manager’s report is an input, not a tax determination.

Before engaging a manager, request a sample report with identifying guest details removed. Check that you can follow a booking to its payout, explain each material deduction and find the supporting record if you need it later. If you are exploring ProHouse management, use the owner enquiry page to discuss scope and reporting expectations rather than assuming a standard package.

title: Can you stay in Wolli Creek and visit Sydney CBD by train?
description: Planning a Sydney visit from Wolli Creek? See which city stations the T4 serves, what to check for your travel date and how to choose a private room.
intro: Yes. Wolli Creek is outside Sydney CBD, but its station is on the T4 route through Central, Town Hall and Martin Place. If you want a private room near Sydney Airport and plan to visit the city, first choose the CBD station closest to your destination. Check the live journey for your dates before booking; the train ride is only one part of the trip.

sections.heading: Which Sydney CBD station should I use from Wolli Creek?
sections.html:
“Sydney CBD” covers more than one destination. Transport for NSW shows the T4 Eastern Suburbs & Illawarra Line serving Wolli Creek, then Central, Town Hall and Martin Place on its city route. Central may suit onward train connections; Town Hall and Martin Place serve different parts of the city. Enter your actual destination in the Transport for NSW Trip Planner rather than assuming every city address is closest to Central.

Check the platform, direction and stopping pattern for the service you choose. Transport for NSW warns that routes can vary by time of day. Wolli Creek has access to the CBD; the accommodation itself is not in the CBD.

sections.heading: How long should I allow from my room to a city appointment?
sections.html:
Plan from the room door to your final address, not just from Wolli Creek Station to a city station. Include the walk to the station, any wait, the train journey, the walk from your city station and a margin for disruptions. A station-to-station estimate cannot promise when you will reach a meeting, attraction or event.

Check current alerts and trackwork on your travel date, especially for late evening and weekend journeys. If your plans have a fixed start time, check both the outbound and return trips.

sections.heading: Can I combine a Sydney CBD visit with an airport stay?
sections.html:
Yes, if the location and room arrangements suit your itinerary. Wolli Creek Station is served by both T4 city routes and the T8 airport route; the stations are different from the property. For the airport, choose Domestic Airport Station or International Airport Station for the correct terminal and check current services. Airport station access fees can affect the total train fare, so compare the full journey before deciding.

Our early flight guide covers airport timing and overnight planning in more detail. This guide focuses on visiting the CBD while staying outside it.

ProHouse offers Room 1, Room 2 and Room 3 as private bedrooms with private bathrooms in a shared apartment. The kitchen and living area are shared. Compare each room’s photos, capacity, bathroom details and availability before selecting it; a room booking is not a whole-apartment booking.

Use the location page to review where the property sits relative to Wolli Creek Station. If your city plans end late, review the self check-in steps in advance. ProHouse has no onsite reception, and pre-arrival approvals are handled during the stated weekday hours.

Use the ProHouse location guide and your selected listing to check the walking route from Wolli Creek Station. Allow additional time for luggage, crossings and finding the entrance. Station-to-property walking time is separate from the train ride.

sections.heading: Where can I stay overnight before an early Sydney Airport flight?
sections.html:
A Wolli Creek room can suit an overnight stay before a flight if its check-in arrangements and your morning transport fit your schedule. Reserve the night before the flight: a flight leaving on Tuesday morning normally means booking Monday night. Choose your actual overnight dates and guest count on the booking page.

Work backwards from the time your airline requires you at the terminal, not just the flight departure time. Include packing, leaving the room, walking to transport, waiting, the journey and reaching the airline’s check-in or bag-drop area. A short rail journey does not mean you can leave the property immediately before your flight.

sections.heading: How long is the train ride from Wolli Creek to Sydney Airport?
sections.html:
For orientation, Rome2Rio lists an indicative train ride of about 2 minutes from Wolli Creek Station to International Airport Station, and about 5 minutes to Domestic Airport Station. These are station-to-station estimates, not a guaranteed timetable or door-to-door travel time.

  • T1 International: use International Airport Station.
  • T2 or T3 Domestic: use Domestic Airport Station and confirm the terminal with your airline.

Use the Transport for NSW Trip Planner for your exact date and departure time. Its current services and alerts take precedence over indicative estimates in this guide.

sections.heading: How long does it take from Sydney Airport to Wolli Creek?
sections.html:
Start by selecting International Airport Station or Domestic Airport Station as your origin and Wolli Creek Station as your destination in the Trip Planner. The T8 airport route connects these stations. Check that your selected service stops at Wolli Creek and follow current platform information.

Your full arrival journey is longer than the train ride. Add time to leave the terminal, reach the station, wait for your service and walk from Wolli Creek Station to your accommodation. For international arrivals, immigration and baggage collection add another variable. There is no single accurate airport-to-room time for every flight and guest.

Transport for NSW confirms that using Domestic or International Airport stations attracts a station access fee in addition to the train fare. Check current fares before comparing the train with a taxi or rideshare; avoid assuming a short train ride means a very low total fare.

sections.heading: Can I rely on the train for a very early flight?
sections.html:
Check the first suitable service for your actual travel date. Do not assume airport trains run all night or that a daytime service pattern applies before dawn. Look for planned trackwork, replacement transport and the terminal arrival time, particularly on weekends.

If the rail timetable does not get you there in time, arrange an alternative such as a taxi or rideshare and allow for pickup and traffic. ProHouse is outside the airport terminals; do not treat it as an airport-terminal hotel or assume an airport shuttle is included.

sections.heading: What should I complete before my overnight stay?

ProHouse uses self check-in with no onsite reception. Check-in begins at 3pm after the required arrival preparation, and approval hours are Monday–Friday, 9am–5pm. Complete identity verification and the required credit card pre-authorisation steps in advance, especially if arriving late or over a weekend. A paid booking alone does not mean unfinished arrival checks can be approved overnight.

Read the self check-in checklist and credit card pre-authorisation explanation. Before bed, keep your departure instructions, luggage and morning transport plan ready. Then your overnight stay supports the flight rather than adding last-minute decisions.

title: Credit card pre-authorisation: why you may not see a refund
description: Understand credit card pre-authorisation (pre-auth), why releasing a pending hold usually creates no refund transaction, and what to check in your banking app.
intro: Seeing an amount disappear from your available balance can feel like you have been charged. It is understandable to look for a refund afterwards. If the amount was only a credit card pre-authorisation (pre-auth) hold and was never charged, its release usually works differently: the pending hold disappears, rather than a separate refund arriving.

sections.heading: The short answer: check Pending, not just Refunds
sections.html:
If your security amount was held but never charged, you will usually not see a separate refund transaction when it is released. Instead, look for the original amount under Pending in your banking app. After your bank processes the release, that pending hold will usually disappear and the held amount becomes available to spend again.

Some banks keep a record marked “reversed”, “cancelled” or similar. The exact display depends on your bank. Check that the pending item has not changed into a completed charge.

sections.heading: What is a credit card pre-authorisation (pre-auth)?
sections.html:
A credit card pre-authorisation, often shortened to pre-auth or called a security hold, temporarily reserves an amount on your card. Think of it as money set aside, rather than money paid to ProHouse.

For a hold that has not been captured as a payment, the held amount has not been transferred to ProHouse. However, you cannot spend that amount while it is reserved. On a debit card this reduces your available funds; on a credit card it reduces your available credit.

sections.heading: Why does it look like money has been taken?
sections.html:
Banking apps often show a hold as a negative amount alongside other transactions. Your available balance or available credit also falls. That can look like a payment even though the transaction is still pending.

Example only: if you have $1,000 available and a $200 hold is placed, you may see $800 available. If the full hold is released without any payment being taken, the $200 becomes available again once your bank updates it. You would not normally see an extra $200 refund entry. This example is not ProHouse’s required security amount.

sections.heading: Release of a hold versus refund of a payment
sections.html:
• Hold released: an amount was reserved but not charged. The held amount is released. A separate refund entry is usually not created.
  • Payment refunded: an amount was actually charged and is then returned. Your bank may show a refund credit or reverse the original payment.
  • Hold captured: some or all of the reserved amount becomes a completed payment. This is different from simply releasing the full hold.

This guide describes an uncaptured security hold, not your accommodation payment. If an amount has become a completed charge, ask us to check that specific transaction rather than assuming it is a released hold.

sections.heading: How to check your banking app
sections.html:
1. Open the card account used for the security pre-auth.
  2. Find the original amount and date in the Pending or authorisations section.
  3. After the release is processed, check whether the hold has disappeared or is marked reversed/cancelled.
  4. Check your available balance or available credit, allowing for other spending and pending transactions.
  5. If the entry has become completed or posted, contact ProHouse so we can check whether a payment was taken.

The disappearance of a pending entry alone does not prove that it was released: it can also disappear when replaced by a completed payment. Check both sections.

sections.heading: Still seeing the hold? Here is what to ask
sections.html:
A release by a business and an update in your banking app may not happen at the same time. Processing depends on your bank, card and transaction; there is no single release time for every guest.

Contact ProHouse if you need us to confirm the pre-auth status for your booking. If we have confirmed release but your available funds have not updated, ask your bank: “Is this a pending pre-auth hold or a completed payment, and when will the released hold stop affecting my available balance?”

You can send us your booking reference, transaction date and amount. If sharing a screenshot, hide your full card/account numbers and unrelated transactions. Never send your card security code, online banking password or one-time passcodes. Contact ProHouse if you would like help checking.

title: Private room or whole apartment for your Sydney short stay?
description: Compare privacy, shared spaces, bathrooms and total booking costs before choosing a private room or whole apartment for a Sydney short stay.
intro: Two listings can show a similar bedroom photograph while offering very different stays. Before comparing prices, establish whether you are booking one room or exclusive use of an apartment. That choice affects privacy, shared facilities and how comfortably the space fits your trip.

sections.heading: Start with what is exclusively yours
sections.html:
A private-room booking gives you the bedroom described in the listing. Other spaces may be shared with other guests. A whole-apartment booking gives you exclusive use of the apartment described in that particular listing; it does not mean exclusive use of the building or its common facilities.

At ProHouse’s Wolli Creek shared apartment, private-room guests have their own bedroom and ensuite, while the kitchen and living room are shared. Check the Room 1, Room 2 and Room 3 pages and your selected booking details for the exact room.

sections.heading: Compare the bathroom as carefully as the bed
sections.html:
“Private room” alone does not tell you whether the bathroom is shared, dedicated or directly connected to the bedroom. Look for the bathroom description, room photographs and any access arrangements. If the wording is unclear, ask before booking.

For a group, also check the number of bathrooms and sleeping arrangements. A room’s capacity is the capacity of that booking, not permission to use the other bedrooms in a shared apartment.

sections.heading: Think about how you will use the shared areas
sections.html:
A shared kitchen can suit a guest who wants to prepare breakfast or a simple meal. It also requires consideration: clear up after cooking, leave space for others and follow the property’s quiet-hours rules. A shared living room is available to other guests too.

If your trip depends on having a lounge, kitchen and several bedrooms entirely to your group, compare whole-apartment options rather than assuming those areas come exclusively with a private room.

sections.heading: Compare the total for the same trip
sections.html:
Use the same dates, guest count and length of stay for each option. Check the final price, cleaning charges, parking arrangements and cancellation conditions. A security pre-authorisation, where required, should be understood separately from the accommodation price.

For a short airport stopover, the arrival process may matter as much as the room. A self check-in property still requires you to complete its preparation steps. Read our self check-in checklist before travelling.

sections.heading: A quick decision checklist
sections.html:
• Is the booking for a room or the whole apartment?
  • Is the bathroom an ensuite, dedicated bathroom or shared bathroom?
  • Which kitchen and living areas are shared?
  • Does the exact bed setup suit every booked guest?
  • Can you complete the arrival requirements before your trip?
  • Have you compared the final price and cancellation conditions?

Choose the space that fits how you will actually stay. You can compare ProHouse stays and then check availability for your dates.

title: A self check-in checklist for your Sydney short stay
description: Prepare your arrival link, identity verification, access instructions and support details before travelling to a self check-in short stay in Sydney.
intro: Self check-in gives you a way to arrive without collecting a key at a reception desk. A smooth arrival begins before you travel: finish the required checks, understand when access becomes available and keep the correct instructions close at hand.

sections.heading: Before booking: check whether the arrival process suits your trip
sections.html:
Read the property’s check-in time, approval hours and support arrangements. An accommodation business can offer self check-in while having limited staff support outside office hours. Do not assume there is an onsite reception or that an unfinished verification can be approved late at night.

ProHouse uses self check-in with no onsite reception. Arrival approvals take place Monday–Friday, 9am–5pm. If you are travelling outside that window, complete the required preparation in advance. Check the airport accommodation page and the instructions sent for your booking.

sections.heading: Before travelling: finish the required steps
sections.html:
Find your pre-arrival email and use its link to complete identity verification, provide your estimated arrival time and finish the required security-deposit steps. Completing a form and receiving approval are different stages; check the status shown for your own booking.

Use the contact details on the official ProHouse website if something is unclear. Avoid putting identity documents or payment details into an unfamiliar link sent by someone claiming to represent the property.

sections.heading: Save the link, not a guessed door code
sections.html:
Keep the same arrival link available on your phone. For ProHouse, access details are released through that link from 3pm on arrival day after the required steps are completed. An empty access section before release time does not necessarily mean something has gone wrong.

Read the full route from the street entrance to your booked room. Building access, a lockbox and a room lock may be separate steps. A map pin or building name alone may not identify the correct guest entrance.

sections.heading: Check your phone and your parking plan
sections.html:
• Charge your phone and keep a way to access your arrival email.
  • Confirm the exact booked address and room.
  • Check the arrival time and when your access details become available.
  • Arrange any required parking before relying on it.
  • Save the property’s official contact information.
  • Read the instructions before you reach the entrance.

Keep access links and codes private. Do not share them publicly or use another guest’s instructions. Parking arrangements are separate from bedroom access; follow the information provided for your own booking.

sections.heading: If you need help on arrival
sections.html:
Check that you are using the right entrance, your own booking link and the instructions for the current stay. Contact the property with a clear description of the step that is not working. Do not send a door code in a public message or review.

ProHouse support outside business hours is limited. Follow the emergency and contact instructions in your arrival information rather than assuming immediate assistance is available. If you have not booked yet, ask about the arrival process before choosing your dates.

title: What to check when choosing accommodation near Sydney Airport
description: Compare terminal access, room type, arrival requirements and total costs when choosing accommodation near Sydney Airport and Wolli Creek.
intro: “Near Sydney Airport” is a useful starting point, but it does not describe the whole journey. The right choice depends on your terminal, transport, arrival time and the kind of accommodation you want. Use these questions to compare your options before booking.

sections.heading: Plan the trip to your terminal
sections.html:
Check which terminal your airline uses and plan the journey from the accommodation’s actual address. A short distance on a map is not the same as a confirmed walking route, train connection or taxi journey. Allow for luggage, waiting and your airline’s check-in requirements.

Use the Transport for NSW trip planner for a journey at the time you expect to travel. Check current fares and services directly rather than relying on an old blog’s exact travel-time estimate.

sections.heading: Choose the accommodation type deliberately
sections.html:
A hotel, a private room in a shared apartment and a whole apartment can all serve an airport trip, but their facilities and service models differ. Check whether reception is onsite, whether common areas are shared and what bathroom arrangement is included.

ProHouse’s Wolli Creek private-room accommodation is in a shared apartment, with private bedrooms and ensuites plus a shared kitchen and living room. It is outside the airport terminals and has no onsite reception. Read our room-versus-apartment guide if you are deciding between booking types.

sections.heading: Match the arrival requirements to your flight
sections.html:
For an early arrival, establish when the room will actually be available. For a late arrival, check whether any identity verification or payment steps need staff approval beforehand. Do not assume self check-in means you can finish every administrative step at any hour.

At ProHouse, check-in starts from 3pm after the required arrival preparation. Approval hours are Monday–Friday, 9am–5pm. Complete the process before travelling, especially when your journey falls outside those hours. Our self check-in checklist explains what to prepare.

sections.heading: Compare the complete stay cost
sections.html:
Compare the same dates and number of guests. Review the final accommodation total, any cleaning charges, transport costs and parking conditions. If driving, check whether parking must be booked separately and whether your vehicle suits the available space.

Read the cancellation conditions that apply to the selected rate. A cheaper room may have different flexibility, while a longer stay can change the importance of kitchen access and shared facilities. Avoid choosing on a headline nightly price alone.

sections.heading: Make the booking easy to follow
sections.html:
Before paying, check the exact room, address, guest capacity and arrival process. Keep the booking confirmation and official contact details together. If staying near Wolli Creek is suitable for your trip, explore ProHouse’s airport accommodation information and check the room details for your dates.

For a city visit as well as a flight, review the Wolli Creek location guide and plan each journey separately. Your best airport base is the one that fits the full trip, not only the nearest-looking map pin.

title: Questions to ask a short-stay property manager before you sign
description: Compare short-stay property management scope, commission, property costs, guest access, maintenance and owner reporting before choosing a manager.
intro: A management commission is only one part of choosing someone to look after your property. A useful comparison sets out who does each job, what it costs and how you will know what is happening. Take these questions into your first conversation with a short-stay manager.

sections.heading: What is included in the management fee?
sections.html:
Ask for a written description of the service. Discuss listing preparation, booking channels, guest communication, arrival arrangements, pricing, cleaning coordination and maintenance reporting. Establish which tasks the manager handles directly and which involve separate suppliers.

For any quoted percentage, ask what amount it is calculated on, whether tax is included and which costs are additional. Compare a realistic example that separates accommodation income, commission, platform costs, cleaning and other agreed expenses. This makes competing proposals easier to understand.

sections.heading: Who pays to get the apartment ready?
sections.html:
Walk through photography, furniture, linen, kitchen equipment and access setup before a launch date is promised. Clarify who chooses items, who approves purchases and who owns them. An onboarding service and the physical items purchased for a property are different costs.

Ask the manager to identify what is essential for opening and what can wait. Agree the scope and budget for your particular home rather than assuming a package covers every expense. ProHouse describes its current approach on the List your home page; confirm the applicable proposal directly.

sections.heading: How will guests arrive and get support?
sections.html:
Ask how guests receive arrival instructions, when access becomes valid and how access ends after a stay. Discuss the backup plan for a lock problem, who receives maintenance reports and how urgent issues are escalated. Keep security details out of public listings.

Also ask about support hours and the difference between emergency assistance and routine enquiries. Clear expectations help you judge whether the service model suits the property and the guests you want to host.

sections.heading: How are cleaning and maintenance decisions handled?
sections.html:
Agree who checks the property between bookings, how problems are documented and when an owner is contacted. Discuss purchase approval limits, supplier invoices and what happens when work cannot wait. Ask how maintenance responsibilities involving the building or strata are identified and escalated.

Before committing, confirm which approvals, insurance arrangements and property-specific requirements need checking with the relevant authority, insurer or adviser. A manager’s marketing proposal alone should not be treated as confirmation that every home is suitable for short stays.

sections.heading: What will I see in my owner reporting?
sections.html:
Ask for an example of the owner statement and how booking income, deductions and payments are explained. Discuss how pricing decisions are reviewed and what data will be available. Treat any income forecast as an estimate with assumptions, not a guaranteed return.

Finally, read the agreement’s provisions for owner use, rate changes, ending the arrangement and transferring listing or access information. Put important answers in the written agreement. To start a ProHouse conversation, tell us about your home, its suburb, bedrooms and current setup.

title: Private room or whole apartment? Keep every booking listing accurate
description: A practical channel-audit checklist for distinguishing private rooms in shared homes from whole-apartment short-stay listings.
intro: A room-type error is not a small wording problem. If one channel describes a private bedroom as an entire home, a guest can arrive expecting exclusive use of spaces that are actually shared. Owners and managers need one accurate inventory record, then a deliberate check of how each booking channel displays it.

sections.heading: Start with the space the guest can use exclusively
sections.html:
Describe the booking from the guest’s point of view. A private-room booking gives the guest exclusive use of the stated bedroom, while one or more common areas are shared. A whole-apartment booking gives the guest exclusive use of the apartment described in that listing.

Do not decide the room type from the building category, the number of bedrooms in the property or a photograph of one bedroom. Record which bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, living and entrance areas are private or shared for that specific bookable unit.

sections.heading: Use each platform’s actual accommodation type
sections.html:
Airbnb describes an entire place as a space where guests have the whole accommodation to themselves. Its private-room type gives the guest a private bedroom with access to shared areas. Those labels set different expectations and should match the stay being sold.

Google’s Vacation Rentals guidance currently says individual rooms and partial homes are not eligible for that integration. A connectivity feed should not convert an ineligible private room into an “entire house” simply to distribute it. Ask the channel manager which inventory types it can transmit accurately, and exclude a listing from an unsuitable feed if it cannot preserve the correct type.

sections.heading: Audit more than the title
sections.html:
Compare the public result with the source listing. Check the property type, room name, guest capacity, bedroom and bathroom count, private-versus-shared facilities, check-in and checkout times, parking, amenities and accessibility information. Confirm that photographs belong to the bookable space or are clearly identified as shared areas.

Review negative amenity labels too. A channel may infer that a feature is unavailable when the source sent no value. Correct the source only when the property information is known; do not add an amenity merely to remove an unattractive “No” label.

sections.heading: Follow the booking link as a guest would
sections.html:
Open the public channel result and follow its booking option. It should reach the intended property or room, not a generic page that makes the guest search again or a different inventory item. Recheck the dates and guest count after the handoff, because a link can be technically live while losing the selected search details.

Then compare the final booking page with the public result: the room type, photos, capacity, bathroom arrangement and main conditions should still describe the same stay. Keep the direct-booking destination on the organisation’s controlled domain or its established booking portal.

sections.heading: Keep an evidence-based channel audit
sections.html:
Record the source listing ID, channel, public URL, date checked, displayed room type and any mismatch. Save a screenshot where appropriate, then make the correction in the source system or ask the connectivity provider to investigate. Recheck the public page after the next confirmed sync rather than assuming that changing one dashboard updated every channel.

For ProHouse, a private room in the Wolli Creek shared apartment is not a whole-apartment booking. The bedroom and ensuite are private; the kitchen and living room are shared. Our stay types show that distinction for guests. Property owners can discuss listing setup and channel management with ProHouse.

title: A practical Wolli Creek stay guide: groceries, food and transport
description: Plan groceries, local food, airport and Sydney CBD transport, and time outdoors during a short stay in Wolli Creek.
intro: Wolli Creek can be a practical base for a Sydney short stay because everyday shops, local food and rail connections are concentrated around the station. It is not in the Sydney CBD or inside the airport terminals, so plan each journey from Wolli Creek and check live information before you leave.

sections.heading: Start with Wolli Creek Station
sections.html:
Wolli Creek Station is served by the T4 Eastern Suburbs & Illawarra Line and the T8 Airport & South Line. Transport for NSW lists city, airport and southern services from the station, but stopping patterns and platform details can change.

Use the Transport for NSW Trip Planner with your actual departure time. It is safer than relying on a fixed travel-time claim, especially around weekend trackwork or timetable changes. ProHouse is in Wolli Creek with access to the Sydney CBD; it is not CBD accommodation.

sections.heading: Buy groceries close to the local centre
sections.html:
For a longer stay or a simple meal, Wolli Creek has two major supermarkets near the station precinct. ALDI’s official store locator lists its Wolli Creek store at 4 Magdalene Terrace. Woolworths lists its Wolli Creek store at 78–96 Arncliffe Street.

Check each supermarket’s official store page on the day for current opening hours and services. Stock and trading hours can change, so avoid planning around an old directory listing. ProHouse private-room guests share the apartment kitchen and should leave common areas ready for the other guests.

sections.heading: Choose food using live listings
sections.html:
The main local retail and dining area is around Wolli Creek Station and Village Square. Rather than relying on a fixed restaurant list, search a live map for the cuisine you want, then confirm the venue’s current hours, menu and booking requirements with the business.

A useful search should match the time you need food: breakfast before an airport trip, a late dinner after arrival or takeaway for the shared apartment. Check the walking route before leaving, and remember that a nearby map result may sit on the opposite side of the railway or a major road.

sections.heading: Plan airport and CBD trips separately
sections.html:
The T8 line connects Wolli Creek with Sydney Domestic and International Airport stations and city stations. Transport for NSW advises that an airport station access fee applies in addition to the train fare when using the airport stations. Opal and contactless payment are accepted, subject to the current fare rules.

For the Sydney CBD, enter your exact destination rather than treating “the city” as one stop. Central, Town Hall and other city locations can require different services or walking connections. Check live service alerts before both your outbound and return journey.

sections.heading: Take a break at Cahill Park
sections.html:
Bayside Council describes Cahill Park as a Wolli Creek park beside the Cooks River, with a playground, seating, barbecue facilities, a sporting field and tennis courts. Facilities or access can be affected by maintenance, events and weather, so check current council information when the park is central to your plans.

For your accommodation, compare the exact room and shared-space arrangement before booking. ProHouse offers private ensuite rooms in a shared Wolli Creek apartment, and its location guide explains the property area and arrival context.
